candidate.answerReason: Unrolling the stripe gives a parallelogram with horizontal base 3 feet and perpendicular height 80 feet, so its area is 240 square feet.

methods.label: Unroll the cylindrical wall
methods.explanation:
Flattening the cylindrical wall makes the stripe's horizontal width useful as the base of a parallelogram.

[Figure 1](figures/2004_AMC_10A_Q19_question_fig1.svg)

Imagine cutting the wall along a vertical line and unrolling it without stretching. If the cut separates the stripe into pieces, move those pieces horizontally by whole circumferences to join them into one continuous parallelogram. Cutting and moving the pieces preserve their total area.

The parallelogram has horizontal top and bottom edges of length \(3\) feet. Their perpendicular separation is the silo's height, \(80\) feet. Therefore the stripe's area is
\[
3\cdot80=240\text{ square feet}.
\]
The two revolutions determine the parallelogram's slant; both are already included in its full height. The answer is \(\boxed{240}\) square feet, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).
methods.levelReason: The method uses elementary cylinder unfolding and the base-times-height formula for parallelogram area.
